purpose: Separate persistent planetary place identity from causally evolving local environmental state.
principle: A place persists; its environmental state changes as a consequence of world conditions.

examples: rain may leave wet ground after precipitation stops
snow may persist after temperature rises depending on accumulated energy and exposure
flooding may persist after the storm moves away
dust and dryness require causal drying history

rules: A climate or biome label supplies context, not an instantaneous weather result.
Environmental state must be temporally continuous unless an explicit event changes it abruptly.
Returning to a known location must load and evolve prior environmental state rather than reroll it.
AI narration may describe authoritative environmental state but cannot invent contradictory weather or terrain.
Exceptional conditions require an explicit cause or generated event.
Simulation LOD may simplify calculations but must preserve causal continuity.
core_rpg_boundary: Generic environmental persistence and causal-state evolution should live in CoreRPG when available; Star Trek owns planetary, technological and setting-specific profiles.
